Occupational Therapists use occupational therapy theory and activity analysis to design training for people with functional limitations caused by injury, illness, development, or aging. They train daily living, work, and leisure skills and use assistive devices and environmental modifications to restore independent living and participation.

paragraphs: At the morning meeting, review new-admission assessments and the previous day's progress. In the morning, lead one-on-one gripping and transfer practice, breaking down each movement. Write assessments and training records at midday. In the afternoon, conduct group training in wards or schools and adjust assistive devices. Before leaving, align the plan with the team and agree on goals for the next day.

In one sentence: help people with functional limitations live independently again. The work includes ability assessment, training plans, daily living skills, assistive devices, return-to-work support, documentation, and collaboration. It engages hands, mind, and emotion.

Employment is projected to reach 182,100 by 2034, a net increase of about 22,100 jobs, with approximately 10,200 openings each year. The median annual wage was about $98,300 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace Occupational Therapists, but it will take over documentation for assessment and records. Digital tools can generate training plans and progress dashboards, but face-to-face manual training, motivation, and functional judgment depend heavily on people. Therapists who can assess, practice alongside patients, and show empathy are more secure, while tools reduce pure form-filling work.

Through daily living training, assistive devices, and environmental modifications, they help restore independent living and working abilities.

This career suits people who combine patience, empathy, and task analysis. Movements must be broken down, progress requires waiting, and people need warmth.

This field depends most on patience, empathy, and the ability to break down movements. A seemingly simple task such as tying shoes can require ten or twenty steps taught slowly. It suits thoughtful people who genuinely want to help and can tolerate slow progress.
Prefers helping others, investigation, and hands-on work (Social S + Investigative I + Realistic R).
If you are thoughtful and genuinely want to help people reclaim their lives, occupational therapy is one of the most human-centered rehabilitation roles.

Physical Therapists manage joint movement, muscle strength, and pain, while Occupational Therapists manage daily functions such as eating, dressing, and working. One restores physical capacity and the other restores daily living ability, and they often work together.
